title: Graphing a Horizontally and Vertically Shifted Cubic
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph and analyze the function y = (x - 1)^3 + 2 by starting with the standard cubic graph y = x^3 and applying appropriate translations.
finalAnswer: \text{Parent } y = x^3 \text{ shifted right } 1 \text{ and up } 2;\quad \text{Inflection point: } (1, 2),\quad \text{Domain: } (-\infty, \infty),\quad \text{Range: } (-\infty, \infty),\quad \text{y-intercept: } (0, 1)

steps.title: Identify the Translations from y = x^3
steps.explanation: Start with the standard cubic curve y = x^3, shift it 1 unit to the right by replacing x with x - 1, and shift it 2 units upward by adding 2.
steps.why: In y = f(x - h) + k, (h, k) = (1, 2) is the translation vector.

steps.title: Locate the Point of Inflection, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: The point of inflection (with horizontal tangent) moves from (0, 0) to (1, 2). Both domain and range are (-infinity, infinity).
steps.why: Cubic polynomials are strictly increasing or decreasing bijections from R onto R.

steps.title: Find the Coordinate Axis Intercepts
steps.explanation: The curve increases through its x-intercept (1 - cbrt(2), 0), crosses the y-axis at (0, 1), flattens momentarily at (1, 2), and rises through (2, 3).
steps.why: Evaluating at x = 0 and solving (x - 1)^3 = -2 gives the exact intercepts.
